articles.headline: SANS ISC posts YARA rule for orphaned VBA macros in DWG files (Oct 18 2026)
articles.dek: A new SANS Internet Storm Center diary entry describes a YARA rule that spots leftover VBA projects embedded in AutoCAD DWG files.

body.text: Key Takeaway

On Oct 18 2026 the SANS Internet Storm Center released a YARA rule that detects orphaned VBA projects hidden inside DWG files — a simple, language‑agnostic filter you can drop into any cloud‑storage scan pipeline. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897][FACT:772d124d895774720ffd03df5fb9c9fb]
Why This Matters

Orphaned VBA code can execute when a DWG is opened by downstream tools, so a malicious macro could steal credentials or drop ransomware into AI‑driven CAD processing jobs. The rule gives defenders a low‑cost way to catch that attack surface before it reaches production. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897]
What Happened

SANS’ diary entry titled “Orphaned VBA Projects Inside DWG Files: YARA Rule” was posted on Oct 18 2026 and includes the full YARA signature and sample metadata. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897][FACT:772d124d895774720ffd03df5fb9c9fb]
Builder View

If your workflow pulls DWG files from cloud buckets for AI feature extraction, add the published YARA rule to your CI/CD scanner or cloud object‑storage malware scan. It runs in under half a second per file and needs no code changes—just an updated YARA rule set. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897]
Open Questions
So far the finding rests on a single SANS diary entry; no independent surveys have measured how common these orphaned macros are in public CAD libraries. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897]
Ardur Take

Treat the rule as a practical early‑warning for any cloud‑native pipeline that ingests DWG files. Deploy it now, watch hit counts, and revisit when Autodesk updates the DWG spec or when broader industry coverage appears. [FACT:07c87fb10b4b147231c878d9d12cb897]

keyPoints: SANS ISC published a YARA rule targeting orphaned VBA macros inside DWG files (Oct 18 2026).
The rule can be added to existing cloud‑security scanners with minimal overhead.
Current coverage is from a single SANS diary entry; broader prevalence data is still missing.
